findings.title: Update invalidation decision uses the org-aware wrapped model, which can skip a needed login-cache invalidation
findings.body: `update()` takes the original IDP from `getById()`, which returns the org-aware wrapper. For an IDP linked to an org, the wrapper's `isEnabled()` also requires the org and the organization feature to be enabled. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then calls `getLoginPredicate().test(original)`, so an enabled IDP in a disabled org looks 'not a login IDP'. The cached login lists are built from the stored attributes (JPA query on `enabled=true` etc.) and still contain that IDP. If the IDP is then updated so that the new state is also 'not login' (for example `hideOnLogin=true`), the early return skips invalidation. The stale entry stays in the cache, and when the org is re-enabled the IDP is wrongly shown on the login page. The comparison should use the unwrapped stored model, for example from `idpDelegate.getById`.

findings.title: Cleanup registered with literal "alias" instead of the created alias, leaking IDPs
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP literally named "alias", not the IDPs created in the loop (`idp-alias-N`). The same bug is at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. None of the 21 IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are cleaned up, and the cleanup itself may fail with 404. Leftover login IDPs can pollute other tests in the same realm, such as the exact counts asserted in this test or `OrganizationCacheTest` reruns. The cleanup should use the actual alias.
